## Recall · Lecture 13

a) What gives an Android Virtual Device its Android version?
b) Which command lists the connected devices and emulators?
c) What can an emulator not test well?

::: {.answer}
a) the system image
b) adb devices
c) the heat of a long race
:::

## Activity 1 · Start and install · 18 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- An AVD is created in the Device Manager of Android Studio, and adb installs the build.
- **Do it:** Create and start P5_API_30. Then run adb devices and adb install PocketQuest_1.3.apk.
- Your product is a running emulator with the game.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/seminar-steps.png)
:::
::::

## Check 1 · Start and install

What shows that the emulator and the install worked?

::: {.reveal}
1. The emulator shows the home screen of Android 11 after a cold boot of about 15–60 seconds.
2. adb devices lists emulator-5554 as a device.
3. adb install prints Success, and the Pocket Quest icon appears.
:::

## Activity 2 · Test case 7 · 15 min

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- Test case 7 says: start a race, then turn the device to landscape.
- **Do it:** Run the test case, read the log and take a screenshot. Then write the bug report with all its parts.
- Your product is one complete bug report.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](images/bug-report.png)
:::
::::

## Check 2 · Test case 7

What does a good bug report of test case 7 contain?

::: {.reveal}
1. The title says what goes wrong: the race freezes when the device turns to landscape.
2. It names the build and the device: PocketQuest_1.3, build 42, on P5_API_30 with Android 11.
3. It gives the numbered steps, the expected result and the actual result.
4. It attaches the screenshot and the log line with RaceHud.cs, line 118.
:::

## Wrap-up

- You can start an Android Virtual Device and install a build with adb.
- You can run a test case, keep the evidence and write a bug report.
